text:
anya: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we hit an edge case in the wild: sampled traces sometimes lose per-request budget when a request is re-routed across shards and a cache-hit happens. That leads to under-attribution in the billing/telemetry pipeline and skews unit-costs for inference routes.

devon: Can you sketch where that "request_budget" would live? Envelope header? trace root? How does it survive sampling and proxies?

anya: Sketch: top-level envelope field called "request_budget" (small numeric, e.g., token-cost units) + optional "consumed_delta" on spans that perform work. Front proxy sets origin_budget. Samplers MUST preserve origin_budget in the sampled root so downstream attribution works. Minimal example: 

```
{
  "trace_id": "e3f1...",
  "request_budget": "0.0125", // token-cost units (string to avoid language float edgecases)
  "spans": [
    {"id":"s1","service":"proxy","consumed_delta":"0.0005"},
    {"id":"s2","service":"model-host","consumed_delta":"0.0120"}
  ]
}
```

marcos: Two practical concerns: (1) if every envelope carries a numeric field we increase indexing/egress cost, and (2) what are merge/overwrite semantics when multiple services alter budget? Also caches: cache-hits currently create almost no instrumentation and we might lose cache-fill cost.

sue: For (2) we can adopt an "origin + deltas" model: front sets origin_budget, downstream services report consumed_delta. Aggregator computes attribution = min(origin_budget, sum(consumed_delta)) and emits reconciled cost. That avoids complex merge conflicts and keeps per-event payload small (one small numeric or absent).

anya: Exactly. Implementation approach: envelope contains origin_budget only. Spans optionally include consumed_delta. Sampler must ensure origin_budget survives sampling even if consumed deltas are sparse. If consumed_delta missing, the aggregator falls back to route-model estimates.

devon: Privacy/compliance check — we're only carrying numeric budgets and tiny ids, no PII, right?

marcos: Correct, numeric only. But be mindful of retention: keeping origin_budget for long traces is harmless, but we should document retention impact.

sue: Cache-fill handling: when cache returns, consumed_delta = 0 on the fast path, but the cache-fill (when it occurred) should emit a separate span/event with the fill's consumed_delta so attribution isn't lost. That keeps the fast path small and accurate.

anya: Sampler rule proposal: when not sampled, drop consumed_delta events but keep origin_budget on the sampled root/head. That slightly increases sample head size but preserves attribution signal. Also add a small sampler whitelist that forces-sample events that report large consumed_delta (>threshold) so we don't miss heavy-cost requests.

marcos: Test matrix to add: missing origin_budget, double-count (two services both report same consumed_delta incorrectly), cache-fill attribution, sampler-drop edgecases. I'll add infra test stubs.

devon: Rollout plan idea: opt-in field stored by region/tenant; ingest config flag to accept/ignore origin_budget. Default disabled for regions where we haven't validated pipeline cost. Also add a gradual rollout and flag to backfill attribution based on stored route-model heuristics. :thumbsup:

anya: I'll draft a short addendum to the RFC with envelope schema, sampler invariant, aggregator pseudo-query and rollout checklist. Ping reviewers when ready. :rocket:

obs-bot: Note: created tracker issue #OBS-842 to capture tests + RFC addendum link.

anya: Thanks everyone — will follow up with the addendum and a small PR for the sampler change.
